title: Prove sharp uniform bounds for triangular parity macro cuts
body:
The triangular Toeplitz parity compiler's one-level bounds do not directly control an unfinished child composed with its ancestor shear. This package proves a sharp, depth-independent common infinity-norm bound of `1/(1−η)` for every prefix, suffix and their inverses at complete-shear boundaries, for every dyadic dimension and every legal interleaving of the disjoint child programs. At tail `l1 ≤ 1/2`, all four bounds are at most **2**. This includes the source's parallel child schedule.

The proof simultaneously inducts on all four cut operators while retaining the shared even/odd coefficient budget. The geometric inverse family proves the common constant is sharp. An exact `N=4` suffix of norm `7/4` shows why a one-level `3/2` cap cannot cover all composed cuts. The sharper **forward-prefix-only `3/2` question remains open**.

This sharpens macro-boundary conditioning within the polynomial stability claim already present in `SHALLOW-TOEPLITZ.md`; it does not replace the internal dirty-shear gate, rounding, full Gaussian, normalization or supplier-admission obligations. No new κ or selected-frontier change.

Validation:

- Python 3.12 registered metadata/source-pin validation and package replay pass.
- Seven exact rational fixtures at `N=1,2,4,8,16`: 116 distinct cut matrices, including all pairs of child cuts for each fixture; all four operators checked.
- Exact suffix witness and geometric inverse checks; four failure controls; direct replay also passes under Python `-O`.
- Committed-byte and declared-source-history publication preflight pass.
- A second Codex agent independently reviewed the proof and checker and used a separate sparse row-action implementation for three interleaving schedules. Root agent reviewed the four block identities and inequalities. These are AI checks, not independent human or maintainer acceptance.

Credit: Vlado Vojdanovski/#1673 for the shallow compiler and Cinna Davis/#4100 for its later caller; Jose Manuel/#4198 for the separate rational-generator work; Ryanson Jonathan's `one-factor-of-t` question and unpaidmoon's #4371; James Reed's #4699 one-level budget and #4701/#4702/#4704/#4705/#4706 finite examples. Exact predecessor heads and source hashes are retained in the package. No unmerged executable dependency is required.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4715 . Base: `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7. Prepared for Brian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
